sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.8% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, reaching $31.7 billion [F198][F9].
Operating income grew faster at a 5.8% CAGR to $8.6 billion, lifting operating margin from 22.9% to 27.2% [F199][F19][F20][F28].
FY2022 revenue jumped 17.1% on higher retail volumes, favorable weather and rate case contributions [D239][P34].
FY2020 net income fell 63.3% to $1.4 billion on coal ash settlement impairments and pandemic-driven volume losses [D157][F33][P60].
Electric Utilities and Infrastructure supplied 90.9% of FY2025 revenue and 3.6pp of its 5.6% growth [D541][D543][D358].
Residential electric was the largest customer class at 43.3% of revenue, adding 2.8pp of growth in FY2025 [D774][D776].
Gas Utilities and Infrastructure grew 27.1% in FY2025, contributing 2.0pp, with Piedmont Natural Gas up 32.1% for 1.7pp [D565][D566][D682][D683].
Operating costs grew 5.3% against 5.6% revenue growth, so revenue grew 0.3pp faster than operating costs [D372][D358][D379].
Diluted EPS rose 10.5% in FY2025 against 9.8% net income growth as the diluted share count rose 0.6% [D362][D360][D374].
FY2025 operating margin of 27.2% was the window high, above the 22.9% median and the 19.7% low [F28][D932][D933][D931].
The margin rose 0.8pp in FY2025 as D&A reached 24.3% of revenue and operating costs lagged revenue by 0.3pp [D370][D341][D379].
In FY2025 net margin of 15.7% sat 11.5pp below the 27.2% operating margin, with interest expense of $3.6 billion and an 11.2% tax rate [F47][F28][D967][X63][D345].
The largest swing was FY2020, when operating margin fell 3.8pp and net margin 9.5pp [D168][D169].
FY2025 operating cash flow of $12.3 billion was 2.48x net income, below the 2.59x window median [F77][D346][D958].
Free cash flow was negative $1.7 billion, a -5.3% margin against a -5.8% median, as capex of $14.0 billion ran at 44.2% of revenue and 1.82x D&A [F97][D343][D939][F87][D342][D348].
FY2022 operating cash flow fell 28.5% as rising fuel costs outpaced recovery, increasing borrowings to finance the undercollection [D244][P36].
Stock-based compensation was only 0.8% of operating cash flow in FY2025 [D349].
Net debt reached $89.6 billion in FY2025, with net cash of -282.3% of revenue against a -235.4% peer median [D352][D353][D969].
That net debt position ranked at the 33rd percentile of three peers, and the current ratio fell to 0.55x from a 0.66x median [D968][F177][D945].
Long-term debt rose 4.9% to $80.1 billion while equity grew 3.4% to $51.8 billion [D368][F187][D367][F197].
Dividends of $3.2 billion in FY2022 exceeded that year's $2.6 billion net income, and the diluted share count rose 4.2% in FY2021 [D234][F35][D214].
The current ratio fell to 0.55x in FY2025, below 1.0x, with $21.0 billion of current liabilities against $11.6 billion of current assets [F177][F157][F147].
A utility funding construction with short-term paper can run this thin, but the cushion against a refinancing squeeze is small [F177].
Net debt rose for a ninth straight year to $89.6 billion in FY2025 from $50.0 billion in FY2016 [R3][D352][D14].
Debt-funded capex is the model here, but the steady climb leaves little room if rates or storm costs rise [D352].
Free cash flow was -0.96x of net income in FY2023, 0.01x in FY2024 and -0.34x in FY2025 [R4][D269][D309][D347].
Persistent negative free cash flow means growth depends on continued access to capital markets [D347].
Whether the FY2026 current ratio holds above the 0.55x FY2025 level, reported in the FY2026 10-K [F177].
Whether operating cash flow to net income recovers toward the 2.59x window median from 2.48x in FY2025 [D958][D346].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue moves back toward the -235.4% peer median from -282.3% in FY2025 [D969][D353].
